cases.thesis: Model quality stopped being the differentiator once every serious player could rent the same frontier capability.
cases.instruction: cut the middle section and land harder
cases.body:
Everyone is still benchmarking models. That was the right thing to measure in 2023 and it is close to noise now.

The capability gap between the top four labs, on the work most companies actually do, has collapsed to something a procurement team cannot detect. What has not collapsed is the gap in who gets to put that capability in front of a user with an existing habit.

That is a distribution question, not a research question. It is also a question with an entirely different answer set: partnerships, defaults, bundling, and the boring work of being pre-installed.

The companies still hiring exclusively against benchmark scores are optimising a variable that stopped moving.
